> The enforcement tool for Canonical-Driven Development (CDD). Audit, generate, and guard your project documentation.

# Architecture

---

## System Overview

DocGuard is a near-zero-dependency Node.js CLI tool. It carries one exact-pinned npm runtime dependency, `@babel/parser`, for AST-accurate JS/TS parsing, and uses the developer's own `python3` (no pip/npm dependency) for an AST-accurate Python tier. Both parsers load **optionally**. Route and schema scanners retain bounded fallbacks; architecture analysis reports Python import coverage as unsupported when the interpreter is absent rather than fabricating a graph. Other language scanners retain their declared regex (beta) scope. It enforces **Canonical-Driven Development (CDD)** — a methodology where documentation is the source of truth. DocGuard audits, scores, and guards project documentation. It generates AI-actionable fix prompts and integrates with CI/CD pipelines.

It targets development teams and AI coding agents that need to maintain documentation quality across projects of any stack (JavaScript, Python, Java, etc.).

## Component Map

| Component | Responsibility | Location | Key Files |
|-----------|---------------|----------|-----------|
| **CLI Entry Point** | Argument parsing, config loading, command routing | `cli/` | `docguard.mjs` |
| **Commands** | User-facing commands (the Daily 5 — init/guard/diff/sync/score — plus situational tools including reconcile, retire, specs, and `init --with` scaffolders) | `cli/commands/` | `*.mjs` |
| **Document lifecycle** | Finds exact terminal-status docs and completed-task review candidates; explicit retirement removes documentation from active context only after its source revision is reachable from a retained Git ref | `cli/scanners/document-lifecycle.mjs`, `cli/validators/document-lifecycle.mjs`, `cli/commands/retire.mjs` | Scanner is read-only; retirement uses the shared multi-file transaction and remains explicit |
| **Spec lifecycle registry** | Projects immutable spec identities, reviewed lifecycle/lineage/scope, artifact digests, task state, qualified implementation/test evidence, bounded outcomes, and recovery tombstones into one byte-stable control file | `cli/scanners/spec-registry.mjs`, `cli/scanners/requirement-evidence.mjs`, `cli/scanners/revision-anchor.mjs`, `cli/validators/spec-registry.mjs`, `cli/commands/specs.mjs` | `specs --write` preserves reviewed fields; stale checks identify bounded field paths and distinguish canonical ordering from changed content; only committed, clean, digest-current lifecycle entries can defer traceability, while a current planned entry that is new, removed from the index, or modified pending commit remains advisory; `specs approve` records approval and a `planned`, `in_progress` or `implemented` delivery and refuses `verified`/`released`; `specs complete` is the only verified-delivery writer |
| **Reconciliation graph** | Inventories changed paths independently from bounded patch text, maps them to direct spec evidence, to a spec whose reviewed `assetPaths` cover them (files that cannot carry an annotation, such as digest-pinned fixtures; spec 039), a deleted file to a current, approved spec that names it (the exact path, or a directory that no longer has tracked files; spec 069), or to a requirement declared in a canonical document (`docs-canonical/<doc>.md#<ID>`), and keeps mechanical facts, approved intent, decisions, unrelated changes, and unsupported evidence separate | `cli/shared-git.mjs`, `cli/scanners/reconciliation.mjs`, `cli/commands/reconcile.mjs` | A patch that overflows or times out in one read is read again in batches of changed paths under the same per-call budget, keeping only per-file facts between batches (`readPatchBatches`, spec 028 FR-008). A batch read that still exceeds a bound, a parse failure, or an incomplete inventory blocks a ready result; planning is read-only and `--write` never rewrites requirements |
| **Analyzer tier** | Decides which analyzer produced each piece of evidence at the two entry points (`parseJsTs`, `extractPythonFiles`), carries `tier`/`tierReason` on scanned items, reports `parserTier` on every finding, and downgrades a validator to `partial` when an AST-capable language was read by the pattern fallback (`regex-fallback`) or when a language with no AST tier was read by pattern (`fallback-language`: Go, Java, Kotlin, Ruby, Rust, PHP, C#). The Environment validator is `partial` when a source language has no env patterns. The symbol map and module graph name the languages the import graph does not read | `cli/shared-source.mjs` (`tierFor`, `summarizeTiers`, `tierApplicability`, `grepEnvUsage`, `LANGUAGE_NAMES`), `cli/scanners/routes.mjs`, `cli/validators/api-surface.mjs`, `cli/validators/environment.mjs` | Findings are retained; only coverage is downgraded. The two tiers give different reasons: a parser was unavailable, or none exists. A package segment (`src/main/java/com/example`, Go `internal/example`) is product code, not an examples directory (specs/043-fallback-language-coverage) |
| **Python web extraction** | One module outline per Python file, from the `python3` AST tier or the pattern tier when no interpreter is available; the resolvers compose FastAPI/Flask router prefixes across modules, follow Django URL configurations from `ROOT_URLCONF` (including DRF router registrations), classify ORM models (SQLAlchemy, Django, SQLModel) with relationship cardinality, and read `BaseSettings` environment variables | `cli/scanners/py-outline.mjs`, `cli/scanners/py-sources.mjs`, `cli/scanners/python-routes.mjs`, `cli/scanners/python-models.mjs`, `cli/scanners/py-env.mjs`, `cli/scanners/py-ast.mjs` | Both tiers share the resolvers, so they differ only in what they can read; pattern-tier facts keep `parserTier: regex-fallback`, lower `generate` confidence and mark their sections partial. Unresolved paths, prefixes and includes are flagged, never guessed, and join the route scan's `unresolved` list so API-surface coverage is `partial` with their count and first location (specs/063-coverage-followups). Schema-Sync reads the same model scanner as `generate` |
| **Spec Kit artifact coverage** | Treats Spec Kit's own documents as governed. Coverage counts top-level `specs/<feature>/**/*.md` and the constitution under a `specKit` tier. Metrics-Consistency (including `MET004` dependency claims) and Reference-Existence read the constitution | `cli/scanners/speckit.mjs` (`findConstitution`), `cli/commands/guard.mjs`, `cli/validators/metrics-consistency.mjs`, `cli/validators/reference-existence.mjs` | The constitution usually lives in a dot directory the walkers skip, so it is located explicitly. Nested fixture `specs/` trees are not the project's artifacts |
| **Headline coverage** | Reports how many validators actually checked beside the passed/total check count, and caps the badge colour at `green` when any active validator was partial, unsupported, missing a prerequisite, or errored | `cli/commands/guard.mjs` (`badgeColor`, `incompleteCoverage`) | `no-matches` keeps the top grade: a validator that ran and found nothing applicable completed its job |
| **Finding channels** | Separates the three questions a finding answers — does CI block (`severity`), who decides (`disposition`), how well is the code measured (`evidence`), and which analyzer produced it (`parserTier`) — so a certain observation is never labelled uncertain and the feedback loop samples the labels that have never been validated | `cli/findings.mjs`, `cli/precision-evidence.mjs`, `cli/writers/sarif.mjs` | Channels are additive to the published finding contract; `confidence` keeps its meaning as the detector's certainty in its own observation |
| **Precision evidence** | Runs labelled synthetic and exact-commit public cases, separates deterministic results from observations, calculates null-safe quality metrics and confidence bounds, compares case-first baselines, persists them in a provenance envelope whose measure (`benchmark-precision`) and caveat are derived from the cases and re-verified on load, and projects per-code evidence into a generated module the CLI quotes at finding time | `benchmarks/`, `cli/precision-evidence.mjs`, `schemas/docguard-benchmark.schema.json`, `schemas/docguard-benchmark-baseline.schema.json`, `schemas/docguard-precision-evidence.schema.json` | External runs are explicit; third-party project code is never executed and disposable checkouts are removed by default |
| **Documentation site and generated references** | `docs/` is the GitHub Pages site (Just the Docs remote theme in `docs/_config.yml`, which Pages builds itself; no build step or dependency in the repository). `npm run docs:reference` renders `docs/reference/findings.md` from the `CODES` and `BLOCKER_CODES` registries and `explain`'s `DISPLAY_NAMES`; `npm run llms` renders `llms.txt`/`llms-full.txt` | `docs/`, `tools/generate-docs-reference.mjs`, `tools/generate-llms.mjs` | `tests/user-docs.test.mjs` and `tests/llms-bundle-drift.test.mjs` fail on a stale generated file and name the command. `docs/` ships in the npm package (PDFs excluded); `tools/` does not (specs/053-user-documentation) |
| **Non-regression budgets** | Compares a PR with its base on one runner: interleaved guard wall time, self-guard error findings, agent-facing output bytes, packed package weight and runtime dependencies, against the ratios and floors in `budgets.json`; `Budget-Exempt` waives one metric with a reason | `tools/budget.mjs`, `budgets.json` | CI `budget` job; development tooling, not shipped in the npm package |
| **Doc dependency lock** | A doc section declares the code it describes (`covers=` on its `docguard:section` marker); `review --accept` records AST or content fingerprints in `.docguard-doc-lock.json`; the Doc-Dependency validator reports a covered symbol whose code changed (DLK001), a dependency that no longer resolves, an unaccepted or orphaned entry, or an unreadable lock | `cli/scanners/doc-deps.mjs`, `cli/scanners/fingerprint.mjs`, `cli/scanners/py-anchors.mjs`, `cli/validators/doc-dependency.mjs`, `cli/commands/review.mjs` | Opt-in by declaration; only `review` writes the lock; runs in `--changed-only` pre-commit mode |
| **Requirement anchors** | Each `@implements`/`@req` tag anchors to the code under it (file, qualified symbol, statement or route) through Babel, one batched `python3` run, or the self-checking pattern lexer; each link carries an exact, a floor and a requirement fingerprint (`dg1:`). `fingerprint.mjs` holds both the doc lock's `doclock-v0` algorithm and the anchors' `v1`. A link whose code changed lists the tests citing its requirement; `testguard-evidence.mjs` reads saved TestGuard evidence to mark one re-verified. `--orphans` lists untagged exported units under governed paths, and dispositions record why one has no requirement. `trace --matrix` exports requirement → anchor → test as CSV or ReqIF 1.2 through `cli/writers/trace-matrix.mjs`. With `anchors.import`, StrictDoc and OpenFastTrace tags are read, never written. The opt-in tree-sitter tier (`ts-anchors.mjs`, `ts-decls.mjs`, `ts-anchors-child.mjs`) refines pattern-tier symbols from hash-pinned artifacts; `tools/anchor-oracle` measures the pattern tier against it in CI. A `docguard:volatile` comment marks its line, and every tier fingerprints what lies wholly on that line as a placeholder, from one set of marked lines per file (`volatileLinesFor`) | `cli/scanners/anchor-tags.mjs`, `cli/scanners/anchors.mjs`, `cli/scanners/pattern-lexer.mjs`, `cli/scanners/anchor-cache.mjs`, `cli/scanners/requirement-docs.mjs`, `cli/scanners/testguard-evidence.mjs`, `cli/scanners/ts-anchors.mjs`, `cli/scanners/ts-decls.mjs`, `cli/scanners/ts-anchors-child.mjs`, `cli/validators/requirement-anchors.mjs`, `cli/commands/anchors.mjs`, `cli/writers/trace-matrix.mjs`, `cli/commands/trace.mjs` | Opt-in (`.docguard-anchor-lock.jsonl` or `anchors.enabled`); `anchors` lists in any project; per-file cache in `.docguard/`, untrusted in CI or when tracked |
| **Version-age note** | Reads the running release's date from the shipped `CHANGELOG.md` heading for exactly its version; when it is more than 14 days old, the guard text footer, the MCP `initialize` instructions and the context pack say a newer version may exist and name `docguard upgrade` | `cli/release-age.mjs`, `cli/commands/guard.mjs`, `cli/commands/mcp.mjs`, `cli/commands/memory.mjs` | No network call; silent when unsure (no CHANGELOG, no heading, bad date, clock before release), in a source checkout, with `DOCGUARD_NO_UPDATE_HINT=1`, and in the guard footer under `CI`; never in JSON, SARIF, JUnit or MCP tool results |
| **Compact guard response** | Projects the full guard result so each fact appears once: findings once, each code's agent-facing evidence once, validator status and counts, each standard applicability reason once; the MCP guard tool's default | `cli/shared-guard-json.mjs`, `cli/validator-coverage.mjs` (`STANDARD_APPLICABILITY_REASONS`), `cli/commands/mcp.mjs`, `cli/commands/guard.mjs` (`--compact`) | A projection, never a recomputation; `detail: "full"` and the CLI's default JSON keep the complete contract |
| **MCP project confinement** | The MCP server serves its `--dir` (else its working directory) plus each `--root`, fixed at startup. A tool call's `projectDir` resolves against the served directory with symlinks followed and must land inside a served root before anything under it is read | `cli/commands/mcp.mjs` (`isWithinRoot`) | Same check over stdio and HTTP; a refused path gets the same error whether or not it exists; a client cannot widen the roots (specs/041-mcp-project-confinement) |
| **MCP doc navigation** | Exact, bounded answers for agents: which doc lines, instruction lines, requirement IDs and covered sections describe a file; a document's outline; one section or the lines around a reference; the task context packet. One reference matcher shared with `trace --reverse` and `impact`; a path or basename matches only as a whole file name | `cli/scanners/doc-references.mjs`, `cli/shared-headings.mjs`, `cli/commands/mcp.mjs` | Read-only; paths pass the evidence reader's checks; 8 KiB default and 32 KiB cap per section read; no tool calls a model |
| **Docs-Sync evidence** | Decides whether a canonical document names a route (DSY001) or service (DSY002) file, reading the documents as a reader sees them: text in HTML comments does not count (comments read through `shared-html-comments.mjs`), a `docguard:section` `covers` entry does. An App Router `route` handler (`app/api/…/route.*`) is named only by the URL path it serves; any other file by the shortest path tail no other checked file shares, matched as a whole word; an `index` or `__init__` file by its directory; a drawn file tree names each entry's path. Messages and warning severities are unchanged. The nudge hook and Diff-Suspicion's `path` kind match whole names the same way (specs 077, 078) | `cli/validators/docs-sync.mjs`, `cli/validators/diff-suspicion.mjs`, `cli/commands/hooks.mjs`, `cli/shared-html-comments.mjs`, `cli/scanners/routes.mjs` | Shared-name decisions are made over every selected file, even under `--changed-only` |
| **Document fidelity** | Keeps the document validators consistent with each other and honest about a blank template (spec 079). ENV001/ENV002 match headings through `docHasSection`, as STR003 does. DDF002 and `diff` expand single-level brace patterns in documented tests (`expandBraces`, at most 64 paths). DDF001 reads a negator over a whole list, removal and migration verbs, and skips change-record sections. A canonical document is an unedited scaffold when its authored lines are all lines of its shipped template: STR006 reports it, docQuality counts none of its checks, and Machine markers does not count it. `countSyllables` reads its exceptions by own property only. | `cli/validators/environment.mjs`, `cli/validators/docs-diff.mjs`, `cli/shared-scaffold.mjs`, `cli/validators/structure.mjs`, `cli/commands/score.mjs`, `cli/scanners/agent-readability.mjs`, `cli/validators/doc-quality.mjs` | `tests/doc-validator-fidelity.test.mjs` |
| **Feedback fixtures** | Validates synthetic reproductions and opposite controls, reduces them under an explicit predicate, derives duplicate identities, and emits test-only contributions | `cli/feedback-fixture.mjs`, `cli/commands/feedback.mjs`, `schemas/docguard-feedback-fixture.schema.json` | Publication remains user-controlled; contribution generation requires reviewed redaction, scope, and benchmark-delta evidence |
| **Evidence-scoped verification** | Binds one exact Markdown statement to a typed JSON Pointer value, bounded file collection, static Python container literal, or saved upstream compatibility report and returns one of five explicit states | `cli/evidence/`, `cli/validators/evidence.mjs`, `cli/commands/verify.mjs`, `schemas/docguard-evidence.schema.json` | Reads stay local, bounded, non-executable, and symlink/private-path safe; direct verification exits 1 for contradiction/invalid input, 2 for unresolved evidence, and 0 only for verified or unconfigured evidence |
| **Managed Git hooks** | Installs bounded DocGuard blocks while preserving user-owned hook commands before and after them | `cli/commands/hooks.mjs` | Reinstall and removal use one outer marker pair, repair nested markers from affected releases, fail closed on enforcement errors, and fall through after success so user postludes execute. A hook owned by husky, lefthook or simple-git-hooks is never written, even under `--force`; the command prints the line to add to that manager. Hooks are written, replaced or removed only in a folder the repository owns (`resolveHooksTarget` in `cli/shared-git.mjs`): a `core.hooksPath` from global, system or command-line config, or one outside the repository, is refused (spec 065) |
| **Readiness assessment** | Combines guard enforcement and optional CI score policy without changing structural score semantics | `cli/assessment.mjs`, `cli/commands/ci.mjs`, `cli/commands/diagnose.mjs`, `cli/commands/report.mjs` | READY requires a passing guard and configured gates; ATTENTION carries advisory warnings; BLOCKED identifies failed enforcement |
| **Task-specific agent context** | Ranks exact task paths, qualified requirements, finding codes, identifiers, and bounded lexical overlap across current governed evidence | `cli/scanners/task-context.mjs`, `cli/commands/agent.mjs`, `schemas/docguard-task-context.schema.json` | Read-only and deterministic; excludes retired, unapproved, digest-stale, private, and unsafe material; abstains on weak relevance and never upgrades prose accuracy |
| **Suppressions** | Parses `.docguardignore` entries with an optional `expires:` day and `# reason`, and applies only the active ones everywhere the file is read; models every native suppression (ignore file, config arrays, inline pragmas, N/A markers, baseline) with its reason and state; the Suppressions validator reports expired, unreadable and (opt-in) reason-less entries (IGN001–IGN003); `docguard ignore --format claimspec` exports the entries whose reason, expiry and scope survive exactly | `cli/shared-ignore.mjs` (`parseDocguardIgnore`), `cli/scanners/suppressions.mjs`, `cli/validators/suppressions.mjs`, `cli/commands/ignore.mjs`, `cli/writers/claimspec-ignore.mjs`, `cli/claimspec-schema.mjs`, `schemas/claimspec/v1/` | Read-only. Expired and unreadable entries exclude nothing. The claimspec schemas are vendored byte-identical and checked by a keyword-limited validator that refuses keywords it does not implement; nothing is exported without a written reason (specs/057-ignore-reasons) |
| **Doc ownership map** | Resolves each tracked file to the one doc section responsible for it (exact path beats glob; longer literal prefix beats shorter), reports unowned code and ties, and lints a committed `.devin/wiki.json` | `cli/scanners/doc-ownership.mjs`, `cli/validators/doc-ownership.mjs`, `cli/commands/trace.mjs` | The map is declared by people in `.docguard.json`; `trace --owners --suggest` drafts one and never writes |
| **Path-scoped agent rules** | Derives each agent instruction file's scope per harness (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, OpenHands) and checks it against the tracked files; `rules --for` resolves what an agent loads for a path | `cli/scanners/instruction-scopes.mjs`, `cli/scanners/frontmatter.mjs`, `cli/validators/path-scoped-rules.mjs`, `cli/commands/rules.mjs` | Tracked files only in guard; formats verified 2026-09-30 and recorded in `docs/ai-integration.md`; patterns DocGuard does not evaluate are reported as not checked |
| **Cross-language import graph** | Resolves repository-local JS/TS and Python static imports for cycle and layer checks, once per run for every consumer. JS/TS imports come from the Babel syntax tree: import declarations of any shape and length (`import type` included), re-exports with a source, `require()`, TS `import = require()`, and, as dynamic edges outside cycle adjacency, `import()` and TS or JSDoc `import('…')` type references; text in other comments and in strings is not an edge. A file the parser cannot read falls back to a pattern whose clause spans lines but never a statement. Every edge carries the tier that read it. It also owns the reverse-import walk (two hops, modules with more than 15 imports excluded) that `impact` and requirement-anchor ripple share, and records the names each import binds, from the same read, so ripple keeps only importers of the changed name. JS/TS aliases resolve through the nearest `tsconfig.json`/`jsconfig.json` (`compilerOptions.paths` and `baseUrl`, following `extends`) | `cli/scanners/import-graph.mjs`, `cli/scanners/ts-paths.mjs`, `cli/validators/architecture.mjs`, `cli/scanners/py-ast.mjs`, `cli/commands/impact.mjs` | Python supports regular flat/`src/` packages and explicit relatives; dynamic imports, runtime path changes, parse failures, missing interpreters, and ambiguous modules remain explicit limitations. A JS/TS file read by the pattern fallback is a limitation too (`js-parser-unavailable` once for all files, or `js-parse-failed` per file), and ARC findings carry the tier of the files they cite (specs/076-js-import-edges). An alias that names no project file adds no edge; configs are read as JSONC, never executed; `extends` stops at depth 8 or a cycle |
| **Symbol map** | `memory --pack --symbols`: ranks source files by PageRank over the cached import graph and lists their exported names within a byte budget; symbols are read only for the files that fit | `cli/scanners/symbol-map.mjs`, `cli/scanners/js-ast.mjs` (`moduleSymbols`), `cli/scanners/py-ast.mjs` | Opt-in by benchmark decision: frozen agent-context protocol v3 (`benchmarks/agent-context/manifest-v3.json`, v2 with only the executable pin changed) computed `opt-in`, with no regression and no predeclared benefit; names only, no claim about behavior |
| **Code-derived diagrams** | Draws the `module-graph` (directory modules and their imports) and `entity-diagram` (schema entities) mermaid sections from code, so GST002 reports drift and `sync --write` redraws them; a graph missing evidence is `partial`, never stale: a missing Python interpreter or JS/TS parser, an unparsable Python file, an unreadable file | `cli/scanners/module-diagram.mjs`, `cli/scanners/memory-plan.mjs`, `cli/validators/generated-staleness.mjs` | Only for a doc that has the marker or is being created; node, edge and depth limits are captioned; hand-drawn diagrams are untouched |
| **Repository-root guidance** | Detects a likely governing ancestor without changing the selected scan directory | `cli/repository-root.mjs`, `cli/docguard.mjs` | Requires ancestor DocGuard configuration or npm/pnpm membership, respects nested Git boundaries, and uses typed stderr diagnostics for machine modes |
| **Lifecycle transactions and context** | Stages registry, recovery, spec outcome, and current-context changes before any visible mutation and rolls the set back on write or validation failure | `cli/writers/file-transaction.mjs`, `cli/writers/spec-outcomes.mjs`, `cli/scanners/lifecycle-context.mjs` | Active context includes approved current spec pointers and content hashes; retired prose is excluded |
| **Adoption baseline** | `guard --update-baseline` freezes the current findings in `.docguard.baseline.json` as fingerprint → occurrence count; guard and `ci` then suppress up to that many of each and gate everything new, reporting how many were suppressed and how many entries are stale | `cli/writers/baseline.mjs`, `cli/commands/guard.mjs` | A fingerprint hashes the code, the location without its line number and the message with digits masked, minus an advisory tail declared per code in `ADVISORY_TAILS` (today only TRC004's IR soft-match hint, which names whichever test file matches best). Guard also accepts the legacy full-message fingerprint so a baseline from an earlier release keeps working; one finding consumes one entry (specs/052-baseline-stable-fingerprint) |
| **Agent instruction budget** | Measures every `AGENTS.md` chain from the root to each instruction directory, as Codex loads it (`AGENTS.override.md` replaces `AGENTS.md`), against `agentInstructions.maxBytes` (default 32768) or a per-chain allowance | `cli/scanners/agent-instructions.mjs`, `cli/validators/structure.mjs` | `STR004` is an escalation; `STR005` suggests tightening a slack allowance. Increasing an allowance is a reviewed config change, which the digit-normalized finding baseline could not guarantee |
| **As-built specs** | `generate --spec <area>` collects deterministic facts under one code area (routes, exported JS/TS symbols, env vars read, entities), renders a Spec Kit spec with one agent-written candidate per fact, and registers it as `origin: as_built` with `sourcePaths`. The Spec-Registry validator re-scans those paths (`SPR007`) | `cli/scanners/as-built.mjs`, `cli/scanners/js-ast.mjs` (`exportedNames`, shared with the symbol map), `cli/commands/generate-as-built.mjs`, `cli/validators/spec-registry.mjs` | DocGuard writes no requirement prose. Facts key on method+path, file+export, name, so line moves never churn them. An App Router handler export is not a second fact beside its route. Route and env facts cite the file and line of the registration or first read. The registry fields are serialized only when set. `--write` commits the spec and its registry entry in one file transaction |
| **Go, Spring and Rails routes** | Reports each route at the path it is served under. Go (gin, echo, chi, fiber, gorilla/mux, net/http): every router value is a node whose prefix comes from `Group`, chi `Route`/`Mount`, gorilla `PathPrefix().Subrouter()` or `http.StripPrefix`, across blocks, functions and files, resolved after every file is read. Spring (Java and Kotlin): class-level and method mappings, including the `path =`/`value =` forms, arrays, constants and `@RequestMapping(method = …)`. Rails: `config/routes.rb` and the files it `draw`s, with `namespace`, `scope`, nested `resources`, `only:`/`except:`, `member` and `collection` | `cli/scanners/go-routes.mjs`, `cli/scanners/spring-routes.mjs`, `cli/scanners/rails-routes.mjs`, `cli/scanners/route-lexing.mjs`, `cli/scanners/routes.mjs` | No parser: a shared lexer masks comments and strings and pairs brackets, so comments, `_test.go` files, HTTP-client calls and Feign clients do not count. Routes carry `parserTier: fallback-language`. A path or prefix that is not literal, or a Go call with several possible callees, places no route rather than a guessed one (specs/047-go-spring-rails-routes) |
| **Sinatra, Starlette, Rust builder, Warp and Tide routes** | Reads the frameworks spec 060 added (#519), and the Actix, Axum and Rocket builders spec 071 composes. Sinatra: classic and modular apps (classes inheriting from `Sinatra::Base` across files), `namespace` prefixes, `register`ed extensions, and the prefixes `config.ru` maps or a host app `use`s. Starlette: `Starlette`/`Router` objects join the FastAPI/Flask graph, with their `routes=` lists, `Mount` children and `add_route`. Warp: filter expressions evaluated to path/method alternatives through `and`/`or`, `let` bindings and functions across files, from what `warp::serve` runs. Tide: `at()` trees and `nest()` mounts resolved after every file is read. Actix, Axum and Rocket: `web::scope`/`web::resource`, `Router::new()` and `rocket::build()` nodes mounted by `.service()`, `.configure()`, `.nest()`, `.merge()` and `.mount()` across functions and files, every method of an Axum method router, and handler macros under the scope or mount that registers them. A Go module with only `net/http` is classified so `go-routes.mjs` runs | `cli/scanners/sinatra-routes.mjs`, `cli/scanners/rust-routes.mjs`, `cli/scanners/python-routes.mjs`, `cli/scanners/project-type.mjs`, `cli/scanners/routes.mjs` | No parser for Ruby or Rust: a tokenizer (Ruby) or the shared lexer (Rust) masks comments and strings first. Ruby and Rust routes carry `parserTier: fallback-language`, Starlette routes the Python tier. A path that is not literal is omitted, and the API-surface coverage reason counts the omissions (specs/060-more-route-frameworks); the builder reader records what it recognised but could not place in `scan.unresolved` (specs/071-real-project-route-gaps) |
| **Laravel, Symfony and ASP.NET Core routes** | Reports each route at the path it is served under. Laravel: the route files the app loads (`bootstrap/app.php` `withRouting`, else `RouteServiceProvider` mappings, else `routes/web.php` and `routes/api.php` under `/api`), with `prefix`/`middleware`/`group` chains and resource expansion. Symfony: `#[Route]` attributes and `@Route` annotations under the class-level route (the route itself on an invokable controller), and `config/routes.yaml` routes and prefixed imports; a declaration no controller reads, and a Laravel route file no application loads, are recorded in `scan.unresolved` (specs/071-real-project-route-gaps). ASP.NET Core: attribute-routed controllers (inherited class routes, verb attributes, `[controller]`/`[action]`/`[area]` tokens) and minimal APIs (`Map*` under `MapGroup` prefixes, followed into the methods a group is passed to). The classifier labels a `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web` project ASP.NET Core | `cli/scanners/php-routes.mjs`, `cli/scanners/dotnet-routes.mjs`, `cli/scanners/routes.mjs`, `cli/scanners/project-type.mjs`, `cli/validators/api-surface.mjs` | No parser: per-language lexers mask comments and strings (PHP `#` comments, heredocs, interpolation; C# verbatim, interpolated and raw strings) and reuse the shared bracket pairing. Routes carry `parserTier: fallback-language`. A path or prefix that is not literal is omitted, counted, and reported in the API-surface coverage reason with its first locations (specs/059-php-dotnet-routes). ASP.NET Core routes carry `caseInsensitive: true`, and `compareEndpoints` (`cli/scanners/api-doc.mjs`) ignores case for them only, as ASP.NET Core does; every other framework compares exactly (specs/063-coverage-followups) |
| **JS/TS extraction** | Route case sensitivity per router (`cli/scanners/route-case.mjs`: each JavaScript framework's router options and app setting, carried down the mount chain, and the NestJS adapter; an unreadable setting compares exactly and is noted, specs/063-coverage-followups); router `.route('/x').get().post()` chains with mount prefixes; per-route auth from the route's own middleware and handler, an earlier `use(auth)`, an auth mount above it, or an App Router `middleware` matcher (a JWT middleware built to let unauthenticated requests through, `passthrough: true` or `credentialsRequired: false`, marks nothing; spec 071); env reads including destructuring, each read site recorded with file, line and default; the App Router `pages/` and `components/` roots; ORM entities (schema files, table builders, document schemas, decorated entity classes with inherited columns, `define`/`init` models) through one discovery (`scanOrmEntities`) that guard's schema check, `generate` and `diff` share | `cli/scanners/js-ast.mjs`, `cli/scanners/routes.mjs`, `cli/shared-source.mjs` (`grepEnvUsage`), `cli/scanners/schemas.mjs`, `cli/validators/schema-sync.mjs`, `cli/scanners/project-type.mjs` | Auth is recognised by name (`requireAuth`, `verifyToken`, `passport.authenticate(...)`, `getServerSession`); text elsewhere in a file never marks a route. A route path that is not literal or a resolvable constant (a runtime template value, a regular expression) is not reported at a placeholder; it goes to `scan.unresolved` and makes the API-surface check `partial`; a path or mount prefix built from same-file or imported `const` strings (through `import` or `require()`) is resolved, and a prefix that cannot be read leaves the routers below it out instead of at the root (specs/064-js-route-shapes). Table schemas come from their ORM config first, else a bounded search; every schema file is read once. The regex fallback reads route chains, per-statement auth, and table and document-schema fields from the same object text; decorated entity classes and model-definition calls are read as decorator and argument text by both tiers and interpreted once; every table, document schema and entity class read records the tier that read it. Framework and ORM names are listed in `docs/commands.md` (`generate`) |
| **NestJS, Workers and router-library routes** | Reports the routes of NestJS controllers (`@Controller` + method decorators under `setGlobalPrefix`, URI versioning and `RouterModule` paths, auth from guards), of a Cloudflare Worker's `fetch` entry (pathname comparisons, `switch`, keyed tables and `URLPattern` in the entry and the modules it imports, methods from the `request.method` checks around them), of the small edge and Node routers (`basePath`, `base`, `prefix`, `route()` and `use(sub.routes())` mounts and application mounts across files, through `import` and `require`, including a module that exports `sub.routes()`, and OpenAPI route definitions whose `{param}` segments become `:param`), and of file-routed edge functions (each `onRequest*` export of a file under `functions/` at the path its location names, with `_middleware` files as auth evidence for the routes below them, kept only where the output directory's include/exclude routing file lets requests reach them; an output-directory worker file replaces that tree and is read as a `fetch` entry). Each reader is a pure function of file contents; `routes.mjs` gives them their files and records each file's tier and every path a reader could not resolve (`scan.unresolved`) | `cli/scanners/nest-routes.mjs`, `cli/scanners/worker-routes.mjs`, `cli/scanners/router-routes.mjs`, `cli/scanners/pages-routes.mjs`, `cli/scanners/js-route-support.mjs`, `cli/scanners/routes.mjs`, `cli/validators/api-surface.mjs` (`routeScanGaps`) | Syntax tree first, pattern fallback per file; routes carry `tier`. A path that is not literal or a constant the reader resolves (same-file; for the router readers also `const` strings imported from project files) is omitted and makes the API-surface check `partial`, naming the framework, count and first location. Durable Object classes, browser `location.pathname` and modules the Worker entry never imports are not read. A router below a prefix that is not literal reports no route. Framework names are listed in `docs/reference/languages.md` (specs/058-js-framework-routes, specs/064-js-route-shapes) |
| **Spec-first gate** | Classifies a change between the merge base and HEAD as covered, exempt, not governed, uncovered or inconclusive. It reads governed paths from `specFirst` and resolves spec references against `specs/*/spec.md` and the registry | `cli/scanners/spec-first.mjs`, `cli/commands/specs.mjs` | Read-only. An unresolved reference never passes. Git or inventory failure is inconclusive (exit 2), never a pass. The PR body arrives as a file |
| **Spec Kit delegation** | The only code that invokes the `specify` CLI: reads its documented `init` options and `--version`, resolves the integration key from `.specify/integration.json` / `init-options.json` / unambiguous agent signals, initializes Spec Kit, registers the packaged DocGuard extension and re-registers it when the registered version differs; writes the extension commands for the `generic` integration, which Spec Kit registers none for | `cli/spec-kit-delegation.mjs`, `cli/ensure-skills.mjs` | Called only by `docguard init` and `upgrade --apply`, and `ensureSkills` runs only from `init` too (the dispatcher installs nothing, so every other command writes only its own outputs, spec 042); argument arrays only; every failure returns a structured result with the CLI's error and a manual command; requires Spec Kit ≥ 0.11.2, the extension's `requires.speckit_version`, read from the manifest as `MIN_SPEC_KIT_VERSION` and checked before initializing or registering (spec 048) |
| **Agent surface** | What the project's agent can run: the active integration's command layout, derived from Spec Kit's install manifest (`.specify/integrations/<key>.manifest.json`); where DocGuard's own skills go; whether each mandatory hook in `.specify/extensions.yml` resolves; and command hints that name a slash command only when its file exists | `cli/agent-surface.mjs` | Read-only. No per-agent table: the file Spec Kit wrote for `constitution` gives the directory, shape and separator. Paths from `.specify/*.json` are checked to stay inside the project before any write (spec 048) |
| **Validators** | Independent validation modules that check specific aspects of CDD compliance — all emitting structured findings with stable codes (the `CODES` registry in `findings.mjs`) | `cli/validators/` | `*.mjs` |
| **Scanners** | Project file scanners for test discovery, route detection, schema mapping, CDK/IaC, doc-tools, integrations, frontend surface, spec-kit, memory-plan, semantic claims, agent readability, and the tech stack (`tech-stack.mjs`: what every ecosystem's manifests and unambiguous source text show, and which absences a manifest proves) | `cli/scanners/` | `*.mjs` |
| **Writers** | Deterministic doc-mutation and output modules — section-addressable edits, mapped-role ownership authorization, mechanical fix registry, API-Reference writer, generate I/O + doc builders (split from generate.mjs), SARIF emitter (no LLM) | `cli/writers/`, `cli/shared-doc-roles.mjs` | Mapped human docs expose only unique `source=code` sections; new or explicitly generated single-role targets permit whole-document writes; whole-document replacements use backups and `--force` cannot grant ownership. `generate --plan --write` goes through `writeOwnedSections`, which skips the backup only for a DocGuard-authored document (generated marker, or an unedited init template) whose every line outside unpinned code-section bodies survives, and never replaces a `source=human` section. Generators and checks share their facts: `collectEnvVars` (env templates plus code reads) in `cli/shared-source.mjs`, and `detectCodeTechnologies` in `cli/scanners/tech-stack.mjs`, which records the file behind each technology: a manifest of any ecosystem, or an unambiguous source-text signal in a product file for the two technologies commonly used without a dependency (specs/061-dogfood-round-2 lists the signals) |
| **Config** | Configuration loading, schema migration, validator policy, and exact finding-code policy | `cli/` | `config.mjs`, `shared.mjs` |
| **Shared** | Cross-cutting utilities — ignore/glob filters (with `DEFAULT_IGNORE_DIRS`, and `isIgnoredDirEntry` skipping a `bin/` only beside a .NET project file), Git-ignore-aware bounded indexing, package capability counts, source-root resolution, Git helpers, declaration-shaped requirement identity parsing, and the shared doc→code trace patterns used by both `trace` and the Traceability validator | `cli/` | `shared-ignore.mjs`, `shared-validator-surface.mjs`, `shared-source.mjs`, `shared-git.mjs`, `shared-requirements.mjs`, `shared-html-comments.mjs` (HTML comments in Markdown, line by line, with code spans as text), `shared-trace-patterns.mjs`, `shared-openapi.mjs` (OpenAPI discovery shared by API-Surface and Docs-Sync), `shared-test-cases.mjs` (declared test-case counts for Metrics-Consistency `MET003`), `shared.mjs` |
| **Templates** | Document skeletons (ARCHITECTURE, SECURITY, etc.) and slash command files for AI agents | `templates/` | `*.template`, `commands/*.md` |
| **Extension** | Spec Kit extension: AI skills, slash commands, bash scripts and workflow hooks, as declared in `extension.yml` | `extensions/spec-kit-docguard/` | `skills/*/SKILL.md`, `scripts/bash/*.sh` |
| **Tests** | Per-validator unit tests + command-level integration tests using `node:test` | `tests/` | `*.test.mjs` |

## Tech Stack

| Category | Technology | Rationale |
|----------|-----------|-----------|
| Language | JavaScript (ES Modules) | Universal runtime, zero-friction `npx` usage |
| Runtime | Node.js ≥ 18 | Native `node:test`, `node:fs`, `node:child_process` |
| Dependencies | **One npm dep** — `@babel/parser` (exact-pinned, optional-load) | AST-accurate JS/TS parsing; minimal, vetted supply-chain surface |
| Optional external | `python3` (the developer's own) | AST-accurate Python route/schema/import parsing; not an npm/pip dependency; import-graph coverage abstains when absent |
| Package Manager | npm | Standard for Node.js CLIs |
| Testing | `node:test` + `node:assert` | Built-in, no test framework dependency |
| Docker | `Dockerfile` (MCP server image) | Published to GHCR for stdio MCP use; HTTP transport is also available with explicit configuration |

### Recognized Config Files

DocGuard recognizes and validates these project config files:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `.docguard.json` | Project-level DocGuard configuration |
| `.docguardignore` | Per-project file exclusions (like `.gitignore`) |
| `vitest.config.ts` / `jest.config.ts` | Test runner config (scanned for custom test patterns) |
| `.storybook/` | Component documentation tool (detected for docs-coverage) |
| `.jules/` | This repo's own Google Jules routines, rules, preflight and environment setup (`setup.sh`); internal tooling, not shipped (spec 067) |
| `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml` | This repo as a pre-commit hook source — consumers reference `repo: raccioly/docguard` to run `docguard-guard` (changed-only) per commit |
| `glama.json` | Glama MCP directory metadata — declares repo maintainers so the Glama listing can be claimed/managed |
| `server.json` | Official MCP Registry manifest (`io.github.raccioly/docguard`) — server name, npm package, stdio transport |

## Layer Boundaries

The architecture separates command orchestration, validation, extraction, output, configuration, and shared utilities. The boundaries below describe responsibilities and permitted dependencies.

| Layer | Contains | Can Import From | Cannot Import From |
|-------|----------|----------------|--------------------|
| **Extension** (`extensions/spec-kit-docguard/`) | AI skills (SKILL.md), bash scripts, hooks, commands | CLI (via npx), Node.js built-ins | Isolated — spec-kit integration layer |
| **Commands** (`cli/commands/`) | User-facing command logic | Validators, Scanners, Writers, Evidence, Shared utilities, Config | Other commands, except the shared internals a command exports for reuse (e.g. `runGuardInternal`) |
| **Validators** (`cli/validators/`) | Independent validation modules | Scanners, Shared utilities, the pure section parsers in `writers/sections.mjs`, Node.js built-ins | Commands, other validators, and any writer that touches the file system |
| **Evidence** (`cli/evidence/`) | Strict manifest loading, exact Markdown selection, file-only adapters, scoped identities | Safe scanner primitives, Shared utilities, Node.js built-ins | Cannot execute project code, external tools, package managers, or network requests |
| **Scanners** (`cli/scanners/`) | Project intelligence — detect routes, schemas, IaC, frontend surface | Shared utilities, the pure parsers in `writers/sections.mjs` and `writers/spec-outcomes.mjs`, Node.js built-ins | Validators, Commands, and any writer that touches the file system |
| **Writers** (`cli/writers/`) | Mutate canonical docs surgically (section-addressable, no LLM) | Shared helpers, Scanners for generated content, Node.js built-ins | Cannot import from Commands or Validators |
| **Shared** (`cli/shared-*.mjs`) | Cross-cutting utilities: ignore/glob filters, source-root resolution, static Worker/Pages binding scopes, git helpers, shared trace patterns | Node.js built-ins plus optional direct parser loading where documented | Cannot import from Validators, Commands, or Writers |
| **Config** (`cli/config.mjs`) | `loadConfig` + defaults/profile merge + project-type detection, which maps the ecosystem profile from `scanners/project-type.mjs` (the detector `init` and `generate` use) | Shared utilities, the project-type scanner, Node.js built-ins | Cannot import from Commands (extracted so `demo`→`docguard` is no longer a cycle) |
| **Entry Point** (`cli/docguard.mjs`) | ANSI colors, argument parsing, command dispatch, banner/help | Commands, Config (`loadConfig`) | Calls validators only through commands |

### Key rule

**Key Rule**: Validators are pure functions. They receive `projectDir` and `config`, then return results. They stay isolated from commands and the CLI entry point. The Extension layer operates independently, using the CLI as an external tool.

```mermaid

    A --> C["Commands<br/>cli/commands/*.mjs"]

    D --> E["Node.js Built-ins<br/>fs, path, child_process"]

```

## Data Flow

### Request Lifecycle: `docguard guard`

```
User runs: npx docguard guard
     │
     ▼
docguard.mjs
  ├── parseArgs(process.argv)      → flags: { format, dir, ... }
  ├── loadConfig(projectDir)       → .docguard.json → merged with defaults
  │     ├── Reads .docguard.json
  │     ├── Reads package.json (name, type detection)
  │     └── Merges: defaults ← config ← CLI flags
  │
  ▼
guard.mjs
  ├── For each enabled validator in cli/validators/ (the list lives in guard.mjs;
  │   e.g. structure, docs-sync, architecture, freshness, doc-dependency,
  │   path-scoped-rules, doc-ownership)
  │
  ├── Collects: { pass: [...], warn: [...], fail: [...] }
  │
  ▼
Output (text | json)
  └── Exit code: 0 (pass) | 1 (fail) | 2 (warn) | 3 (errors, but project not initialised)
```

### AI Fix Flow: `docguard fix --doc architecture`

```
fix.mjs
  ├── Looks up DOC_EXPECTATIONS['docs-canonical/ARCHITECTURE.md']
  ├── assessDocQuality(content, expectations)
  │     └── Checks: line count, placeholder count, content quality signals
  ├── Outputs: TASK, PURPOSE, RESEARCH STEPS, WRITE THE DOCUMENT
  │
  ▼
AI Agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, etc.)
  ├── Reads stdout (the research instructions)
  ├── Executes research: reads package.json, scans directories, maps imports
  ├── Writes docs-canonical/ARCHITECTURE.md with real content
  │
  ▼
docguard guard → validates the newly written document
```

## Key Design Decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|----------|-----------|
| **Minimal dependencies** | One exact-pinned, vetted runtime dep (`@babel/parser`) earns its place by fixing silent regex truncation; it loads optionally so installs stay robust. Everything else is Node.js built-ins. |
| **Config-driven validation** | `.docguard.json` lets projects customize which validators run. A CLI project can skip database docs. |
| **Validators are independent** | Each validator is a self-contained module. Adding a validator keeps existing ones stable. |
| **AI as author, CLI as orchestrator** | The CLI detects problems and generates structured prompts. Documentation writing is the AI's responsibility. |
| **Exit codes for CI** | `0` (pass), `1` (fail), `2` (warn), `3` (errors in a project with no `.docguard.json`) enables `docguard ci` to gate deployments. `3` stays non-zero so an any-non-zero gate is unchanged, but it lets the generated Git hook distinguish "never adopted DocGuard" from "failed its checks". |
| **Scoped factual evidence** | `.docguard-evidence.json` declares narrow, typed source-to-statement predicates. Contradictions fail guard; stale, inconclusive, and unsupported evidence stays visible. A verified statement never exempts its document from freshness or semantic review. |
| **Evidence before context volume** | `agent --task` returns a bounded retrieval packet only after the frozen evaluation showed equal hidden-test safety and lower steps/latency. It remains opt-in because uncached token use increased and the synthetic protocol does not establish universal benefit. |

---

## External Dependencies

DocGuard declares one exact-pinned runtime dependency, `@babel/parser`. It loads optionally: installations without Babel use a less precise regex fallback. The modules below supply the remaining runtime functionality.

| Module | Usage |
|--------|-------|
| `node:fs` | File system operations (read docs, check existence) |
| `node:path` | Path resolution and manipulation |
| `node:child_process` | Git operations, the optional `python3` AST tier, the opt-in tree-sitter anchor tier's `node --no-addons` child, the optional `specify` CLI (`init` and `upgrade --apply`), `npm install -g` for `upgrade --apply`, `git`/`gh` for `upgrade --pr`, `gh` for `impact`, and re-running the CLI itself (`fix`, `diagnose`). All take argv arrays; see SECURITY.md |
| `node:url` | ES Module URL resolution |
| `node:crypto` | Content hashes: doc-lock and requirement-anchor fingerprints, registry and evidence digests, plan- and anchor-cache identity, tree-sitter artifact checks |
| `node:http` | The opt-in MCP HTTP transport (`mcp --transport http`) |
| `node:readline` | Interactive prompts (init command) |
| `node:test` | Built-in test framework |
| `node:assert` | Test assertions |
| `node:os` | Temp directory for tests |

**Dev dependencies**: None. Tests use `node:test` (built-in since Node.js 18).
