## docs-canonical/SECURITY.md
> Authentication, authorization, secrets management, and security policies

# Security

<!-- docguard:quality negation-load off — prohibitions define security boundaries -->
<!-- docguard:version 0.18.0 -->
<!-- docguard:status active -->
<!-- docguard:last-reviewed 2026-10-13 -->

## Overview

DocGuard's validation and extraction run on the local machine. They inspect repository content and return findings. The version-age note (spec 038) reads only the `package.json` and `CHANGELOG.md` shipped with DocGuard and the local clock; the one command that contacts a registry is `docguard upgrade`, when the user runs it. Agent integrations inherit the permissions and data-handling policy of the calling agent. A generated prompt does not authorize a network request, a code edit, or publication.

The optional MCP server supports stdio and HTTP. Installation, upgrade, publishing, and user-opened feedback links may access external services. Local analysis requires no hosted AI service.

## Authentication

| Surface | Authentication | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| CLI and stdio MCP | Calling operating-system user | Local filesystem permissions; MCP tool calls are also confined to the served directories |
| HTTP MCP | Optional API key on loopback; mandatory for non-loopback binding | Host binding, key check, browser-origin validation, and served-directory confinement of `projectDir` in `cli/commands/mcp.mjs` |
| GitHub feedback | User-controlled browser session | Submission occurs only when the user submits a reviewed issue |

The MCP server serves the directory it was started for (`--dir`, else its working directory) and each directory named with `--root <dir>`. The operator sets these at startup; a client cannot widen them. A tool call's `projectDir` is resolved against the served directory, with symlinks followed and letter case as the filesystem stores it, and must land in a served directory or below one. Any other `projectDir` gets an error result that names the served directories, before anything under it is read, and the same error whether or not the path exists. This applies to every tool that takes `projectDir`, over stdio and HTTP. The four documentation tools (`docguard_docs_for_path`, `docguard_doc_structure`, `docguard_read_section`, `docguard_task_context`) return document text, not only findings. Inside a served directory they read through the same safe reader, which refuses `.env*`, `.local`, traversal and symlinked paths, and they bound each answer (8 KiB by default, 32 KiB at most). Serve only the trees clients may read; `--root /` serves everything the account can read. Run the server under an account with only the intended filesystem access. An API key does not provide per-project authorization or a multi-tenant isolation boundary: every client of one server sees every served directory. Network exposure needs deployment-specific access controls.

## Authorization

| Role | Permissions | Responsibilities |
|---|---|---|
| Developer | Operating-system read/write permissions | Review generated changes and opt into mutation commands |
| CI | Workflow token and checkout permissions | Apply the configured gate to the tested revision |
| AI agent | Host-granted tools and permissions | Treat project content as evidence; obtain required authorization for external actions |

Git hooks provide local enforcement and can be bypassed by Git options. Protected merge policy supplies the central enforcement boundary. The shipped hooks prefer an installed local tool and fail when an enforcement runtime cannot execute. Reminder hooks remain best-effort.

A line marked `docguard:volatile` is outside requirement-anchor change detection: whatever lies wholly on it is fingerprinted as a placeholder, so later edits there never turn a link suspect. The marker cannot be added silently. It replaces the line's code in the fingerprint, so adding or removing it turns a reviewed link over that line suspect, and a reviewer sees the marker in the diff. An anchor made only of marked lines is listed as ANC011 (`docguard.volatile-anchor-lines`).

## Secrets Management

Core CLI analysis requires no API credential. Source scanners inspect usage patterns; environment values must not be included in generated public feedback. The optional HTTP MCP API key is supplied by its operator. Keep deployment credentials outside repository content and restrict access to process arguments and logs appropriately.

Evidence verification reads only repository-relative regular files. It rejects
absolute paths, traversal, backslashes, NUL, `.local`, `.env*`, and symlinks;
per-file, aggregate byte, declaration, input, collection, and report limits
bound work. The oasdiff and Buf adapters consume saved outputs and current input
hashes. They never invoke those tools, execute project code, install packages,
resolve remote references, or make network requests. A clean saved report is
evidence only for its declared command, producer metadata, inputs, and selected
statement. Machine output omits raw source values so a mistaken JSON Pointer
cannot copy a secret into CI logs or an agent transcript. Values remain in
process only for typed comparison and non-reversible identities.

The `python-literal-count` adapter tokenizes one bounded Python source file in
JavaScript. It never starts Python or imports the target module. It accepts one
direct module-level static container assignment and returns unsupported or
inconclusive for comprehensions, unpacking, aliases, concatenation, conditionals,
duplicate assignments, malformed syntax, and parser-budget exhaustion.

Reconciliation invokes Git with argument arrays and disables text conversion.
Changed-path inventory and patch text have separate budgets. Any timeout,
overflow, parse failure, or path-limit breach returns partial coverage and cannot
produce a ready claim. Instruction-pointer indexing rejects traversal, private
paths, symlinks, and ambiguous basenames and never follows a match outside the
selected repository.

Task-context selection reuses the same bounded safe reader. It accepts at most
2,000 normalized task characters, stores only the task digest in output, and
does not execute project code, hooks, package managers, an LLM, or network
requests. Eligible prose is limited to configured canonical documents, approved
current specs whose recorded digest matches, and bounded project rules. `.local`,
environment files, traversal, backslashes, symlinks, oversized files, retired or
unapproved specs, and stale registry artifacts never enter selected content.

Feedback issue URLs contain allowlisted detector metadata, classification, parser tier, and a synthetic-shape duplicate identity. Full local finding records can include private paths and diagnostic text. Fixture manifests are accepted only with explicit synthetic-content and redaction-review attestations; they reject escaping paths, `.git`, `.local`, symlinked inputs, unsafe config values, and oversized content. Preview mode avoids all writes. Generated tests contain the attested synthetic fixture, so users must review it before contribution.

The optional external benchmark accepts only credential-free public HTTPS Git URLs pinned to full commit hashes. It disables interactive Git authentication and global/system Git configuration, forbids the file protocol, never runs project scripts, copies no `.git` metadata into case projects, and removes its temporary root by default. External execution is absent from ordinary tests and package installation.

## Subprocess Safety

Pass untrusted arguments through argv arrays and validate values for their intended operation. Avoid interpolating configuration or repository content into shell commands. Existing static command strings do not authorize expanding their input surface. Regression tests in `tests/security-init-injection.test.mjs` exercise the input boundary. `cli/spec-kit-delegation.mjs` is the only caller of the `specify` CLI, and only `init` and `upgrade --apply` reach it: it passes argv arrays (on Windows, `cmd.exe /c specify.cmd` with the same array), accepts an integration key only if it matches `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,32}$`, uses only the `init` options `specify init --help` documents, and bounds each call with a timeout. Its other calls are `specify --version` and `specify extension add <packaged extension> --dev`.

Every other subprocess also takes an argv array and no shell:

- Git: `ls-files -z --cached` / `--deleted` (tracked files), `check-ignore --no-index -z --stdin` (paths go through stdin, never the command line), `cat-file -e` with a regex-validated revision, and `rev-parse` (`cli/shared-git.mjs`, `cli/scanners/doc-deps.mjs`, `cli/scanners/revision-anchor.mjs`, `cli/commands/review.mjs`). Reconciliation's `diff` calls pass `--no-ext-diff` and `--no-textconv`, so no configured diff driver runs; when one read overflows, `readPatchBatches` repeats it with the changed paths after `--` under `--literal-pathspecs`, so a file name is never read as an option or a pattern, and each call keeps the per-call byte and time budget (`cli/shared-git.mjs`, spec 028 FR-008). `ls-files -z -- .docguard` with that fixed path tells the anchor cache whether its state directory is tracked, and if so the cache is not used (`cli/scanners/anchor-cache.mjs`). A saved TestGuard report is untrusted input: its revision reaches `cat-file -e` and `show <rev>:<path>` only after matching the commit-id pattern, and its paths and the claims file's are read through the evidence reader (`cli/scanners/testguard-evidence.mjs`). DocGuard never runs TestGuard or a test.
- The opt-in tree-sitter tier (`cli/scanners/ts-anchors.mjs`) runs `node --no-addons` on one fixed script, `ts-anchors-child.mjs`, with no environment, file content on stdin and a timeout. It runs only when `anchors.treeSitter.artifacts` names the files, never by detection.
  - Each file is read once, and its sha256 must equal the hash `schemas/docguard-anchor-treesitter.manifest.json` pins. The manifest covers the `web-tree-sitter` and grammar versions vetted in `tools/anchor-oracle/VETTING.md`.
  - Those same bytes are written to `.docguard/ts/<sha256>/`. The child imports the runtime from that copy by absolute file URL and loads each grammar from its bytes, so module resolution never runs and a project's `node_modules` cannot supply code.
  - A mismatch, a missing file or a failed child is ANC010, and the pattern tier answers.
- `python3 -c` with one fixed script (`cli/scanners/py-anchors.mjs`) that receives file CONTENT as JSON on stdin, never a path, and only calls `ast.parse` and `tokenize` on it, never importing or executing it. One run per batch, with a timeout of 15 seconds plus 1 second per 64 KiB of input. The doc lock and requirement anchors share it; doc-lock paths are checked by the doc lock's path guard before they are read. `cli/scanners/py-ast.mjs` runs one fixed extractor script that reads file paths on stdin, parses each with `ast.parse` and never imports or executes them, with a 30-second timeout; the import graph, the symbol map and the Python route, model and environment scanners share it.
- `upgrade --apply` runs `npm install -g docguard-cli@latest` when npm has a newer release (on Windows through the shell, with the same fixed arguments, because `npm` is a `.cmd` shim), and `upgrade --apply --pr` runs `git` and `gh` to open the schema-migration pull request (`cli/commands/upgrade.mjs`).
- Development only: `tools/budget.mjs` runs `node` and `npm pack --dry-run --ignore-scripts`.

Only two shell strings remain, and both are static: `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` (`cli/shared-git.mjs`) and `which specify` / `where specify` (`cli/ensure-skills.mjs`).

Paths that come from documents or configuration are checked before use. A `covers=` target must be relative, without `..` or a symlink, resolve inside the project, and respect `.docguardignore`. An `ownership` pattern with `..` or an absolute prefix is an error (OWN007). `rules --for` refuses an absolute path, `..`, and a symlink that leaves the project. Instruction-scope discovery reads at most 200 files and walks at most 100,000 entries without following links.

## Command Safety Levels

Only `init`, and the aliases that run it (`setup`, `agents`, `hooks`, `badge`, `llms`, `publish`), installs DocGuard's agent skills and slash commands or prints the Spec Kit setup hint; `upgrade --apply` refreshes copies that are out of date. They go where the project's agent reads them: the skills directory in Spec Kit's install manifest, else a known integration folder (`.claude/skills/`, `.cursor/skills/`, `.agents/skills/`), else `.agent/skills/` and `.agent/commands/`. A directory read from `.specify/*.json` must stay inside the project. No other command installs them, in any mode, and an unknown command name writes nothing. Read, report, check and preview modes leave the working tree unchanged. The only place they may write is DocGuard's own state directory, `.docguard/`, which ignores itself: each writer creates `.docguard/.gitignore` containing `*` when it is missing and keeps an existing one. DocGuard's dirty-tree checks (`memory --pack`, `report`, `reconcile`, `specs complete`) leave `.docguard/` out. The requirement-anchors cache (`.docguard/anchors.cache.json`) is a speed-up that can never vouch for code it did not see. It is keyed by the sha256 of each file's working-tree bytes, it is not trusted in CI (`CI` set) or with `--no-cache`, and it is ignored, and reported as ANC010, when git tracks any file under `.docguard/`, because a cache forced into the repository could otherwise make changed code read as current.

Git hooks are written, replaced or removed only in a hooks folder the repository owns: `.git/hooks`, or a `core.hooksPath` from the repository's local or worktree configuration that points inside it. `hooks` (including `--force` and `--remove`) and `setup` refuse a `core.hooksPath` from the global, system or command-line configuration, or one outside the repository, because every repository using that folder would run the change (spec 065).

| Operation | Source writes | Auxiliary writes / effects |
|---|---|---|
| guard, score, diff, diagnose | None by default | Plan caching may write into the self-ignoring `.docguard/`; explicit mutation flags change behavior. `guard --update-baseline` writes `.docguard.baseline.json` at the project root |
| ci | None | Records history unless `--no-history` is set |
| feedback | None | Saves local records or an explicitly requested direct `tests/*.test.mjs` contribution unless `--preview`; prints opt-in URLs but never submits |
| memory --pack | None | Writes a generated context pack unless `--stdout` is used; `--symbols` adds a bounded symbol map |
| agent, agent --task | None | Emits a task graph or transient bounded context; never stores raw task text or selected output |
| fix --write, sync --write | Targeted documentation edits | Mapped human documents permit only unique `source=code` sections; backups and fix history remain enabled where supported. `sync --write` skips a section drawn from incomplete evidence unless `--allow-partial` |
| review --accept, review --prune | `.docguard-doc-lock.json` only | One file transaction; `--accept` requires a reason. Plain `review` and `review --suggest` write nothing |
| anchors, anchors --orphans | None | Read-only listings; the per-file cache under `.docguard/` is the only thing written, and only outside CI |
| anchors accept, anchors disposition | `.docguard-anchor-lock.jsonl` only, plus `.gitattributes` with `--gitattributes` | One file transaction; a reason of 10 to 500 characters; `--bulk` for more than one entry; `accept` refuses when a selected file changed during the run. DocGuard authenticates nobody: review the lock through CODEOWNERS |
| rules --for, trace --owners [--suggest], ignore | None | Read-only, including agent skills and the Spec Kit hint; `--suggest` prints a draft ownership block and never writes configuration; `ignore --format claimspec` prints its document to stdout |
| reconcile | None by default | `--write` delegates only mechanical generated-section refreshes to `sync` |
| specs, specs preflight, specs require | None for check/plan modes | `specs --write` refreshes the registry; `specs approve --write` records a reviewed approval and delivery state in the registry only; `specs complete --write` transactionally records a reviewed outcome and active context; `specs reanchor --write` moves recorded outcome revisions in the registry |
| verify --evidence | None | Reads the strict local manifest, selected Markdown, source files, and saved reports; guard consumes the same evaluator |
| retire --write | Explicit clean tracked documentation only | Requires retained-ref recovery proof, clean replacement/evidence docs, and no live Markdown backreferences |
| init, generate | Documentation and configuration scaffolding | Explicit force options may overwrite content. When `specify` is installed and Spec Kit is not initialized, `init` runs `specify init --here --force` (skip with `--no-spec-kit`) and registers the packaged extension. `generate --spec --write` adds one spec and its registry entry in one transaction |
| hooks | Hook configuration and executable scripts | Inventory distinguishes managed, legacy, foreign, missing, and unreadable hooks; removal preserves foreign commands around a managed block; auto-fix hooks may edit and stage documentation. A foreign hook is skipped under `--force` and no `.bak` is written, so overwriting one requires `--force` twice rather than a plain re-install. A hook owned by husky, lefthook or simple-git-hooks is never written, even under `--force`. An installed hook skips a working tree with no `.docguard.json` and permits guard exit 3, so a branch or worktree that never adopted DocGuard is not blocked by a repo-wide hook |
| report | None by default | `--out` writes an artifact |
| trace --matrix | None by default | `--out` (or `--output`) writes the export through the safe write, which backs up an existing file |
| upgrade | None by default | Contacts the npm registry unless `--schema-only`; `--check-only` only reports. `--apply` installs the newer CLI globally, migrates `.docguard.json`, refreshes out-of-date agent files and re-registers the Spec Kit extension when its registered version differs; `--pr` puts the migration on a new branch and opens a pull request instead of editing in place |

Review the exact command and flags before assigning privileges. CLI help is the authoritative command inventory.

Mapped paths do not weaken the write boundary. A new target or an existing
`docguard:generated true` file can receive a single-role full-document write;
otherwise only an exact code-owned section can change. The command validates
all mapped targets before its first visible write, rejects malformed or shared
ownership, and treats `--force` as overwrite intent rather than authorization.

## Supply Chain

The package declares one exact-pinned dependency, `@babel/parser`, with its transitive Babel dependencies recorded in `package-lock.json`. AST extraction degrades to a regex fallback when Babel is unavailable. Python AST extraction optionally uses the installed `python3` runtime. No additional runtime package is introduced by the trust improvements. tree-sitter is not a dependency. `tools/anchor-oracle/` is a CI-only tool outside the package's `files`, with its own lockfile. Every package in it is vetted in `VETTING.md`, and it installs with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`. A user who enables the tree-sitter tier supplies the artifacts, and DocGuard loads them only when they match the shipped manifest.

Cloudflare binding extraction reads source and Wrangler file presence only. It
does not load configuration, import application modules, contact Cloudflare, or
read binding values. AST trust requires an official handler/export/import/class
signal and lexical identity; similarly named local objects do not grant binding
status. The parser fallback discloses unsupported class, Pages, and imported-env
forms instead of treating their absence from the inventory as proof.

Repository-root guidance reads only bounded ancestor metadata: regular
`.docguard.json`, `package.json`, and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` files, plus Git's
reported working-tree root. It does not execute package managers or project
code, follow manifest symlinks, scan outside the selected Git boundary, or
change the directory passed to a command.

Dependency audit results are time-specific observations. Run the current audit and supported Node-version matrix before release; a historical clean audit is not a continuing guarantee. Pin third-party CI actions to verified commit SHAs and install from the lockfile. The release workflow's `publish-homebrew` job holds the only stored release secret, `HOMEBREW_TAP_DEPLOY_KEY`, a write deploy key scoped to `raccioly/homebrew-tap`. It checks the downloaded npm tarball against `dist.integrity` and pins GitHub's SSH host keys before pushing.

No workflow job runs code beside a token that can write to the repository. Every workflow defaults to `contents: read`, and a job that writes asks for its own scope. A job that runs the test suite or DocGuard on itself holds no write permission and checks out with `persist-credentials: false`, because a bot may merge new test files without a maintainer (spec 067). A job holding `contents`, `actions`, `pull-requests` or `issues` write runs no package manager, build tool or test: the release assets (Spec Kit ZIP, Claude Desktop bundle, PyPI distribution) are built in read-only jobs and handed over as workflow artifacts, the scheduled release cuts and tests in read-only jobs and pushes the exact patch it validated from a job that runs only `git`, `gh` and `jq`, and the GHCR job logs in only after building and smoke-testing the image. The publishing jobs hold only their registry credential (`id-token` or `packages`). `tests/workflow-permissions.test.mjs` fails any workflow that breaks these rules (spec 068).

## .gitignore Audit

Exclude `node_modules`, environment values, generated build output, and private local files from version control. `.docguardignore` controls analysis coverage separately; it is not a secrecy boundary for every tool that runs in the repository.

A `.docguardignore` entry can end: `expires:YYYY-MM-DD` keeps it through that UTC day. An expired entry, or one whose expiry is not a calendar date, excludes nothing, so the Security validator scans the paths it hid again; guard reports IGN001 or IGN003. `securityIgnore` patterns carry no reason or expiry; `docguard ignore` lists them with every other suppression.

## Security Rules Checklist

- Validate subprocess inputs at their call boundaries.
- Preserve provenance checks before mechanical edits.
- Keep private diagnostics separate from public feedback payloads.
- Treat submitted reproductions as untrusted data.
- Require credentials for non-loopback HTTP MCP binding.
- Disclose unknown or unsupported verification instead of asserting success.
- Verify protected merge policy independently of local hook installation.

## docs-canonical/TEST-SPEC.md
> Test coverage requirements, testing strategy, and quality rules

# Test Specification

<!-- docguard:version 1.4.6 -->
<!-- docguard:status active -->
<!-- docguard:last-reviewed 2026-10-13 -->

> DocGuard has a single optional-load npm dependency (`@babel/parser`) and an optional `python3` AST tier. CLI integration tests cover the full stack with `node:test` (zero dev dependencies) and exercise both AST extractors (`js-ast`, `py-ast`) plus their regex fallbacks. The Python AST tests skip themselves automatically on a machine that lacks `python3`.

| Metadata | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Status** | ![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-active-brightgreen) |
| **Project Type** | CLI |
| **Test Framework** | `node:test` (built-in) |
| **Test Files** | `tests/` |

---

DocGuard's tests verify command behavior through subprocess execution. Command tests run the full CLI binary as a subprocess, capturing stdout and checking output patterns. This approach tests the complete stack in a single pass: argument parsing, config loading, validator execution, and output formatting.

Tests are designed to be config-aware. They verify that project-type settings like needsEnvExample and testFramework correctly influence scoring and validation behavior. Regression guards preserve known failures with dedicated assertions and neighboring valid cases.

All tests use the built-in node:test framework with zero test dependencies. CI runs the suite on Node 18, 20, 22, and 24. Its runtime budget catches a test that runs away (spec 051 FR-007, revised 2026-10-13):
- `tools/suite-runtime-budget.mjs` divides each top-level test's duration by the run's speed factor. That factor is the median ratio of the run's tests to `tools/suite-runtime-reference.json`.
- It fails any test over `TEST_CEILING_MS` (100 seconds at reference speed, in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`).
- The suite total is reported, not gated. Runner speed alone moved it between 188 and 369 seconds for identical code.
- `tests/release-cut-green.test.mjs` keeps the ceiling above the slowest recorded normal test and below a 165-second runaway on the slowest recorded runner.

Local timing depends on runtime and filesystem. Record measured timing with its environment rather than asserting a universal duration.

Test names follow the pattern: "verb + expected behavior" (e.g., "runs and shows a score", "respects projectTypeConfig"). Each test should isolate its mutable fixtures and clean up its resources.

Fixture git is independent of the machine's git config (spec 066). A test that builds or inspects a throwaway repository passes `FIXTURE_GIT` from `tests/helpers/git.mjs` on every git call (hooks off through `core.hooksPath` set to the null device, commit and tag signing off), or calls `fixtureGit()`, which also throws with git's stderr when a setup step fails. The options travel with each invocation and stay out of the environment, so the product code under test still meets the ambient config; `cli/` uses them only for a scratch repository DocGuard creates itself (`docguard demo`). A fixture that depends on a branch name pins it with `git init -b`. `tests/test-git-hermeticity.test.mjs` reports any git spawn in `tests/` that bypasses the helper; an exemption carries a `fixture-git-exempt:` comment with its reason. The CI `hermeticity` job first proves its config is in effect, then runs the suite under it: every hook fails, signing is mandatory through a gpg that always fails, and the default branch is `trunk`.

## Test Categories

| Category | Framework | Location | Run Command |
|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|
| Unit | node:test | tests/ | `npm test` |
| CLI Integration | node:test | tests/ | `npm test` |

> **CLI integration tests cover command routing; packed adoption tests cover the
> release boundary.** Source-tree subprocess success does not prove that npm
> contains every linked or imported file, that remediation is actionable, or
> that an existing repository remains unchanged during inspection.

All test files live in `tests/` and match the glob `tests/*.test.mjs` — the test runner supplies the current inventory as the suite grows; see the Source-to-Test Map below for the source→test traceability that matters.

## Coverage Rules

| Metric | Target | Current |
|--------|:------:|:-------:|
| Command Coverage | Every public command | Scenario coverage; inspect tests before claiming exhaustive behavior |
| Validator Coverage | Every validator | Positive, negative, and regression cases |
| Flag Coverage | Risk-based | Tested scenarios; no exhaustive coverage claim |
| Test Count | — | Current count is emitted by `npm test` |

Completion tests cover initial `implemented → verified` delivery, evidence and
dirty-tree blockers, living-spec `verified → verified` maintenance, and refusal
of empty repeats driven only by generated lifecycle artifacts.

> **Note**: `watch.mjs` is an interactive file-watcher (uses `fs.watch` + process signals). It is
> covered by automated lifecycle tests, including filesystem watcher error handling.
> `tests/watch-reliability.test.mjs` drives the 500 ms debounce with an injected fake clock
> (`runtime.setTimeout` / `runtime.clearTimeout`) and captures console output, so its coalescing and
> queued-check assertions are driven by a fake clock and hold under any machine load (spec 055). The spawn
> tests in `tests/commands.test.mjs` cover real `fs.watch` events and real timers end to end.
> Manual checks supplement platform-specific event behavior.

> **Note**: `tools/budget.mjs` compares guard wall time between two trees. `tests/budget.test.mjs`
> decides every guard-time verdict on a scripted timing source (the `sample` option of `guardPair`):
> seeded load bursts, a 30% slowdown, the interleaving order and a steady drift, so no assertion
> depends on machine load (spec 062). One test spawns real stub trees and asserts only that each
> median is at least the stub's busy-wait. The CI `budget` job exercises the real path on every PR.

## Trust regression scenarios

`tests/score-assurance.test.mjs` checks that structural grades never claim factual verification and that CI, diagnose, and reports retain this boundary. `tests/feedback-contributions.test.mjs` checks confident-finding selection, preview behavior, and outbound metadata privacy. Cache tests must change source contents without changing a manifest or Git HEAD, including repeated edits and fresh-process reads. Hook tests execute generated scripts against controlled runtimes rather than merely matching shell text. Traceability tests pair synthetic fixture IDs with genuine requirement annotations.

A detector fix should include a clean near-miss and a real defect. Held-out neighboring cases are required to evaluate generalization. `benchmarks/baseline.json` is the reviewed reference: 26 measured cases across 13 repository groups plus one explicit unsupported case. Its observed perfect point estimates retain Wilson confidence limits and do not establish exhaustive correctness. The envelope's `review.measures` is `benchmark-precision` and its `review.caveat` must accompany any quoted number; tests assert the committed metrics and caveat are recomputable from the committed cases, and that a hand-edited ratio, stale caveat, or pre-provenance envelope is rejected.

The finding shape is itself a contract, because findings are copied verbatim into shareable feedback records. `tests/precision-evidence.test.mjs` pins the exact key set a guard run emits, so a field added without a specification fails the suite; it also asserts that `location` is a string or null and that `disposition` and `evidence.status` hold values from their declared vocabularies. `tests/findings-channels.test.mjs` pins the derivation rules for the three channels: `disposition` from `suggestion.kind` with `escalate` as the fail-closed default, `evidence` projected per code and always standing alone, and `reportable` true for an unmeasured code even at high confidence. A malformed `suggestion.kind` must omit the suggestion, so a typo stays visible as a missing suggestion instead of reclassifying a fix as a review.

Retirement tests use disposable Git repositories and verify both sides of the boundary: completed planning material is reported for review, while active neighboring material stays clean. Write-path tests must prove retained-ref recovery metadata and refusal of source code, dirty, untracked, required, symlinked, private, protected, submodule, and out-of-root paths. Read-only plan and check modes must not modify repository state.

## Enterprise precision regressions

Regression cases are synthetic and name no consumer repositories. Keep a valid near-neighbor beside every detected defect: formatting versus declaration deletion; negated versus current technology use; explained versus unexplained skips; mock expectations versus credentials; implemented versus omitted contract endpoints; Worker bindings versus local variables; historical versus active documents. Check coverage tests distinguish unsupported and missing inputs from executed checks. Document-role tests exercise mapped findings, raw/loaded configuration parity, unsafe paths, read-only planning, successful section-bounded generation/sync/repair, backup creation, multi-target preflight atomicity, and force-resistant malformed/shared ownership.

Worker fixtures reproduce Cloudflare's module-handler argument, exported Pages
context, imported global `env`, and entrypoint-class property forms. Every form
has a lookalike source, class, function, shadow, or computed-key control. The
packed-package test runs without installed Babel and requires AST-only forms to
remain disclosed as limitations.

JS/TS import-edge fixtures read every import form at the syntax-tree tier
and at the pattern fallback, both in an unparsable file and in a copy of
`cli/` that cannot resolve `@babel/parser`. Controls put each form in a
comment, a string and a template literal, and follow a side-effect import with
a quoted statement the fallback must leave intact. A repository test requires
an edge for every multi-line import and re-export in `cli/`.

Python import-graph fixtures cover regular flat and `src/` packages, absolute
and explicit-relative imports, cycles, and configured layer violations. Paired
controls keep standard-library and third-party imports out of the local graph;
dynamic imports, `sys.path` mutation, parse failures, interpreter absence, and
ambiguous workspace modules must remain partial or unsupported applicability.
Tests never import or execute fixture modules.

Repository-root fixtures pair ancestor DocGuard, npm workspace, and pnpm
include evidence with explicit-dir, local-config, exclusion, Git-only, and
nested-repository controls. Command tests require the selected package result to
remain unchanged, human guidance to contain an exact rerun, and machine stdout
to remain parseable while stderr carries the typed diagnostic.

Independent review must challenge suppression paths, not only the original false-positive example. Cross-project runs use disposable snapshots and verify consumer content remains unchanged. Finding counts alone cannot establish precision or recall.

Task-context tests require exact path and qualified-requirement priority,
determinism, fixed excerpt/read budgets, stale and retired lifecycle exclusion,
private/symlink rejection, honest abstention, aligned human/JSON output, and
unchanged task-graph behavior. The frozen agent benchmark keeps hidden
evaluators outside copied repositories, proves original fail-to-pass and
pass-to-pass states plus reviewed references, records all 27 observations, and
applies its committed non-inferiority and efficiency gate without an LLM judge.
Protocol v2 (spec 036) is frozen beside v1 rather than replacing it: six tasks
(three on the 29-module `ledger-service` fixture), three context conditions
(task only, context pack, context pack with symbol map) and three repetitions,
so 54 trials.
The runner refuses to start when a task's fixture or evaluator digest, or the
manifest digest, differs from the committed value. v2 was frozen with a CLI
version and model that ChatGPT-account Codex no longer serves, so protocol v3
changes only that executable pin, and the runner rejects a v3 manifest that
differs from v2 anywhere else. The v3 trials are recorded in
`results/observed-v3.json`, and a test recomputes their decision (`opt-in`)
from the recorded trials.

Run `node benchmarks/run.mjs --baseline benchmarks/baseline.json` for the network-free synthetic corpus (CI does this on every push; pinned public baseline cases are reported as `outOfSelection`, not as removed). Run `node benchmarks/run.mjs --external --baseline benchmarks/baseline.json` explicitly for pinned public sources. The comparator gates new case-level false positives, false negatives, removals within the selection, and supported-case abstentions. Persisted cold/warm timings are observational because matching Node and platform metadata cannot exclude host contention. Runtime regression claims require at least five controlled samples from the same paired comparison session and a greater-than-20-percent real-workload change.

Evidence adapter tests use paired valid and invalid fixtures. They cover RFC
6901 escaping and array indices, strict typed values, duplicate-free sets,
bounded collections, saved clean and non-clean oasdiff/Buf reports, malformed
reports, unknown adapter versions, input-digest staleness, missing and ambiguous
Markdown targets, unsafe paths, and stable identity behavior. Integration tests
confirm that guard, JSON, SARIF, JUnit, score assurance, agent context, and direct
CLI exit codes retain the five-state boundary. Contradicted and invalid direct
verification exits 1; stale, inconclusive, and unsupported evidence exits 2;
verified evidence exits 0. No test invokes third-party project code or an
external compatibility binary.

Python literal evidence adds paired list, tuple, set, dictionary, annotated,
multiline, string/comment, dynamic, duplicate-assignment, malicious, symlink,
and explicit-budget fixtures. Tests assert that project Python is never
executed. The packed adopter workflow starts with a foreign hook and a
specification missing immutable metadata, runs the installed CLI, validates
every rendered suggestion, follows the proposed remediation, and requires the
post-action registry check to pass.
Managed-hook tests reinstall into a hook with commands on both sides, require
exactly one marker pair, repair nested markers emitted by affected releases,
execute every successful postlude, and retain fail-closed exits. Spec-registry
tests require stale JSON and text output to identify bounded field paths,
including order-only canonicalization.

Express route fixtures pair real registrations with chained HTTP-client calls,
same-path test requests, conventional test-helper trees, single-level mounts,
and nested imported mounts. They also cover static path constants, pathless
mounts, aliased router exports, trailing middleware, and multiple router symbols
in one module. Non-product evidence is rejected before route-key deduplication
so a discarded test call cannot hide a later product route.

Go, Spring and Rails route fixtures are eight reference projects (gin, echo,
chi, net/http, gorilla/mux with fiber, Spring in Java and in Kotlin, Rails).
Each ground truth was written from the framework's routing rules before the
scanner was changed, and the scanner must report exactly that set. Neighbouring
cases cover router names reused in two functions, same-named methods told apart
by package and receiver type, cyclic calls, HTTP-client calls, comments,
`_test.go` files and Feign clients. Prefixes that cannot be read must yield no
route at all.

Sinatra, Starlette, Warp, Tide and `net/http`-only Go route fixtures are five
reference projects run end to end from framework detection, each with a ground
truth written from the framework's routing rules before its reader existed
(all five reported no route before). Neighbouring cases cover Sinatra apps
resolved through project superclasses, `use` and `Rack::URLMap`, Rack::Test
calls, heredocs and `=begin` blocks; Starlette at both Python tiers and a
`Router` from another library; Warp alternatives that cannot match; Tide
bindings reused in two functions; and non-literal paths, which must be omitted
and counted in the API-surface reason.

API omission tests preserve documented endpoints across generated and human
documents, mapped roles, and forced writes whenever the only runtime-absence
evidence is a bounded scan. Field-replay controls pair historical and current
metrics, package capability and enabled-project validator counts, multiline and
disconnected skip reasons, repeated and unrepeated test credentials,
package-local and ignored environment templates, ignored and nested-checkout
pointer copies, committed and non-clean planned lifecycle registries,
authoritative and stale OpenAPI copies, parameter-equivalent and different
routes, frontend utilities and real services, and known versus unknown validator
schema keys.

## CHANGELOG.md
> Version history and release notes

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Changed

- **The CI test runtime budget checks each test, not the suite total**
  (`specs/051-release-cut-green`, FR-007 revision).
  - **Why the total failed.** The 465-second total had been raised three
    times. Across 445 recent CI jobs, identical code ran 188–369 seconds: the
    spread is one speed factor per runner, not the code. The total also missed
    the class it exists for. Test files run about 2.8 at a time, so a test that
    gains 165 seconds (PR #328) adds about 59 to the wall clock. Replayed on
    all 445 jobs, the 465-second total caught none of those runaways.
  - **The new check.** `tools/suite-runtime-budget.mjs` reads the suite's TAP.
    It divides every top-level test by the run's speed factor, measured
    against `tools/suite-runtime-reference.json`, and fails any test over
    `TEST_CEILING_MS` (100 seconds at reference speed).
  - **Measured.** It passes all 445 recorded jobs: the slowest normal test is
    56.9 seconds at reference speed, 1.76× below the ceiling. It catches a
    165-second runaway in one test in all 445, whether the runaway scales with
    the runner or not.
  - **Unaffected by growth.** Adding tests does not change the check.
  - **Reported, not gated.** The suite total goes to the log and the job
    summary.
  - **TAP artifact.** Each leg uploads its TAP as `test-tap-node-<version>`,
    the input for refreshing the reference.

### Fixed

- **Five validator defects reported against 0.45.0** (`specs/079-doc-validator-fidelity`,
  issues 584–588). Four remove false statements; one stops a blank template
  from scoring as finished.
  - **ENV001 and ENV002 match headings as STR003 does** (FR-001). `## Setup steps`
    and `## Environment variables` were "missing" although sentence case passed
    STR003. Both validators now use `docHasSection`: any case, section
    numbers, synonyms (`Getting Started`, `Env Vars`, `Configuration`).
    Findings only disappear.
  - **A brace pattern documents the files it expands to** (FR-002).
    `` `src/tests/{alpha,beta}.test.ts` `` and `` `foo.{test,spec}.ts` `` expand
    one level (at most 64 paths) in DDF002 and `docguard diff`; a missing
    expansion is reported by its expanded path.
  - **DDF001 reads negation over a list and removal verbs** (FR-003–FR-005).
    `no CDK, Terraform or Pulumi stacks`, `We removed Terraform`, `migrated off`,
    `was replaced by` no longer count as documenting the technology, and a
    Revision History, Changelog or Release Notes section is not read as a
    Tech Stack claim. `replaced MySQL with PostgreSQL` keeps PostgreSQL live.
  - **An unedited scaffold is reported and not scored as readable**
    (FR-006–FR-009). New warning STR006: a canonical document that holds
    nothing beyond the template `init` wrote it. Its docQuality checks all
    fail, ALCOA+ Legible is a gap, and Machine markers does not count it. A
    one-document project with a blank template scored docQuality 100%; it now
    scores 0%. A placeholder owner or status alone is not reported
    (`generate --plan --write` leaves both); `<!-- docguard:section scaffold n/a — reason -->`
    owns an intentionally blank document.
  - **The word `constructor` no longer makes readability `NaN`** (FR-012). The
    syllable counter read `Object.prototype.constructor` from its exception
    dictionary, so DQ004 and DQ005 fired on any document containing the word.

- **A living spec reviewed long ago can complete its maintenance again**
  (`specs/028-completion-revision-anchoring`, FR-008–FR-010). Completion
  reconciles from the spec's recorded revision, and `reconcile` read that
  range's whole patch in one Git call capped at 5 MB. Spec 028's own
  maintenance, recorded 83 commits before 0.45.0, was BLOCKED ("Patch exceeded
  its byte budget") with no way forward. A range whose single read overflows
  or times out is now read again in batches of changed paths, each under the
  same 5 MB budget (a rename's two paths together, every path literal), keeping
  only each file's derived links between batches. Coverage is complete and the
  classifications match one unbounded read; `range.batches` reports the reads.
  The range from spec 028's recorded revision (763 files, 7.2 MB) now
  reconciles in 4 batches. A range past every bound (one file's patch over
  5 MB, 64 MB in total, two minutes, or the 5,000-file inventory) stays
  BLOCKED and names the bound or the file.
- **`specs complete --since` no longer skips reviewed history silently.** With
  a recorded revision, `--since` replaced it unconditionally, so a newer ref
  dropped the commits in between from reconciliation and the outcome recorded
  nothing about it; `--help` described the flag as used only when no revision
  is recorded. The same or an older ref is accepted. A newer ref on `HEAD`'s
  history is accepted only when the recorded range is BLOCKED by a budget even
  in batches, and the outcome then records `narrowedFrom` (`revision`,
  `since`, `skippedCommits`, `reason`) in the registry, and the spec's outcome
  line says `Not reconciled: <revision>..<ref>`. Any other `--since` — newer
  over a reconcilable range, unrelated to the recorded revision, or with a
  recorded revision that does not resolve (which names `specs reanchor`) —
  blocks with SPC006 and writes nothing. A spec-text amendment alone still does
  not qualify a living spec for maintenance; the source, test or canonical
  change that implements it does.

## [0.45.0] - 2026-10-13

### Added

- **Requirement anchors: a tag now points at the code under it, not the whole
  file** (`specs/070-requirement-anchors`, user story 1).
  - **Scope by position.** A tag anchors to the narrowest scope its position
    allows:
    - a tag in the file's leading block covers the whole file;
    - a tag directly above a function, class, method or top-level variable
      covers that symbol, by qualified path (`Cart.total`, `Server.Run`);
    - a tag inside a function body, or above another top-level statement,
      covers that statement;
    - a tag above an Express-style registration covers the route
      (`route:POST /login`);
    - a tag inside a Python docstring covers the docstring's owner.

    A file header sitting directly above a declaration stays file-scoped and
    is reported ambiguous, never silently reinterpreted.
  - **`docguard anchors` and the `docguard_anchors` MCP tool.** Both list every
    link, with the tier that placed it:
    - Babel for JS/TS;
    - one batched `python3` run for Python;
    - a string-aware, self-checking pattern lexer for Go, Rust, Java, Kotlin,
      C#, PHP, Ruby, Swift, C and C++;
    - file tier for YAML and shell.
  - **Opt-in for guard.** Guard reports anchors only once a project opts in
    (`anchors.enabled`, or the anchor lock that the next story adds):
    - **ANC007**: a tag cites a requirement nobody declares;
    - **ANC010**: a file was read below its exact tier.

    Projects that have not opted in see no new findings.
- **Reviewed requirement links turn suspect when the code or the requirement
  changes** (`specs/070-requirement-anchors`, user story 2).
  - **Lock.** `docguard anchors accept` records a review in a committed
    `.docguard-anchor-lock.jsonl`, one link per line so reviews on two
    branches merge with `merge=union`.
  - **Accept rules.** An accept:
    - is bound to the exact fingerprints it saw, so a later change flags
      the link again;
    - records the fingerprints it replaced;
    - needs a reason of 10–500 characters;
    - needs `--bulk` for more than one link;
    - refuses when a file changed during the run.
  - **Adoption.** `--baseline` stamps every link as baselined, never as
    reviewed, and the baselined share is reported. `--remove` deletes an
    entry.
  - **Guard findings:**
    - ANC001: a link whose code changed (formatting, comments and line moves
      do not count);
    - ANC002: a link whose requirement text changed (whitespace does not
      count);
    - ANC003: a reviewed link whose tag is gone;
    - ANC005: an unreadable lock, which fails;
    - ANC008: a tag citing a retired requirement;
    - ANC009: two different lock lines for one link after a merge.
  - **What DocGuard does not do.** It edits `.gitattributes` only with
    `--gitattributes`, and it authenticates nobody. CI recipe 3f shows how
    to require human review of the lock through CODEOWNERS.
- **A reviewed link fails guard only where the signal is proven**
  (`specs/070-requirement-anchors`, user story 3).
  - **Policy.** Under `anchors.failOn: reviewed-exact`, ANC001 and ANC003
    are errors for links that:
    - someone accepted as reviewed (never merely baselined);
    - sit at symbol, statement or route scope;
    - were read by Babel or python3's `ast`.

    Every other anchor finding warns, and a requirement-text change never
    fails.
  - **How the default was chosen.** `tools/anchor-churn-replay.mjs`
    replayed 150 commits of this repository: 1,058 flags, all from commits
    that changed code, none from formatting-only ones. `reviewed-exact` is
    therefore the default, and a test keeps the shipped default equal to the
    committed evidence.
  - **Completion.** `specs complete` no longer counts the completing spec's
    own failing anchors toward SPC007; it lists them with their accept
    commands.
- **A renamed or moved function keeps its review**
  (`specs/070-requirement-anchors`, user story 4).
  - **Moved.** The anchor fingerprint leaves out the symbol's own name, so a
    function renamed or moved with an unchanged body is reported as moved,
    not lost and unreviewed. The next accept rewrites its lock key.
  - **Lost.** Two identical candidate bodies, or a changed body, leave the
    old link lost (ANC003). DocGuard does no similarity matching.
- **See what else an anchored change may affect**
  (`specs/070-requirement-anchors`, user story 5).
  - **What is listed.** When an anchored function's code changes,
    `docguard anchors` lists the anchored links in files that:
    - import that file and use the changed name (named, default or
      `ns.name`);
    - sit one import further, at low confidence.

    Hub modules are excluded, and more than `anchors.fanOutLimit` files
    collapse into a count. It is advisory only.
  - **Shared walk.** The reverse-import walk and hub rule moved from the
    `impact` command into `cli/scanners/import-graph.mjs`, so `diff --since`
    and ripple share one implementation; `impact`'s output is unchanged.
  - **Edge names.** Import-graph edges now record the names each import
    binds.
- **Requirement anchors: the tests of a changed requirement need
  re-verification** (`specs/070-requirement-anchors`, user story 6).
  - **Listed.** Under each link whose code changed, `docguard anchors` names
    every test that cites the requirement, as `⊢ test` lines and `tests[]` in
    JSON.
  - **Re-verified from saved TestGuard evidence.** A test is re-verified only
    when all of these hold:
    - the evidence revision carried the anchored code at today's fingerprint;
    - a claim names the requirement as `req:<spec-id>#<requirement-id>` (the
      structured `source.ref` TestGuard validates);
    - the test defended that claim;
    - every fault was killed, with the claim, targets and defenders unchanged
      since the probe.
  - **Inconclusive.** An unreadable, provisional, foreign-revision or stale
    report is inconclusive, never re-verified. A claim that names the
    requirement by file path gets the `req:` form to write.
  - **Reads files only.** DocGuard reads `anchors.testguard.evidence` and
    `anchors.testguard.claims` and never runs a test or TestGuard.
  - **ANC002 data.** Requirement-side findings now carry `scope` and
    `reviewedState`, like ANC001.
- **Requirement anchors: code that implements no requirement**
  (`specs/070-requirement-anchors`, user story 7).
  - **`docguard anchors --orphans`** lists each exported or top-level function,
    class, struct, enum or top-level method that no tag anchors, once, in file
    and line order. It reads under `anchors.orphanPaths` or the current specs'
    `scope.sourcePaths`; `--spec` narrows to one spec. Each language keeps
    its own idea of private: `_name` in Python, lowercase in Go, Rust without
    `pub`, `static` in C.
  - **`docguard anchors disposition`** records why one implements no
    requirement (`derived`, `dead` or `infrastructure`, with a 10–500
    character reason) in the anchor lock. `--file … --bulk` covers a file,
    and `--remove` deletes one. A disposition whose symbol is gone is listed
    as stale. No requirement text is proposed and no model is called.
  - **Granularity.** `score` and `trace` report links by scope and tier as
    information, once a project has opted in.
- **`docguard trace --matrix` exports the requirement → anchor → test chain**
  (`specs/070-requirement-anchors`, user story 8).
  - **CSV.** Fixed, documented columns: requirement, fingerprints, spec state,
    file, anchor, scope, tier, link state, review revision and date, and the
    test with its status. Rows are in UTF-8 byte order, quoted per RFC 4180,
    and a cell that could run as a spreadsheet formula gets a `'` prefix.
  - **ReqIF 1.2.** `--format reqif` holds requirements, anchors and tests as
    spec objects, with `implements` and `verifies` relations, hash-stable
    identifiers and a fixed creation time, so two runs give the same bytes.
  - **Output.** `--spec` keeps one spec. `--out` (or `--output`) writes
    through the safe write, which backs up an existing file.
- **Requirement anchors read StrictDoc and OpenFastTrace tags**
  (`specs/070-requirement-anchors`, user story 9).
  - **Opt in.** `anchors.import: ["strictdoc", "openfasttrace"]` reads
    `@relation(REQ-1, scope=function)` and `[impl->dsn~name~3]` tags as
    anchors to the requirements `anchors.importMap` names, so existing tags
    gain content-based suspect detection without being rewritten.
  - **Findings.** An unmapped ID is ANC007. Native and imported tags for
    different requirements on one symbol are ANC006. An OpenFastTrace tag
    behind the mapped revision is an outdated, code-side suspect (ANC001,
    `cause: "oft-outdated"`).
  - **Cache.** The import settings are part of the anchor cache's identity,
    so editing the map is never answered from the cache.
- **Requirement anchors: provably deterministic fingerprints, and an opt-in
  tree-sitter tier** (`specs/070-requirement-anchors`, user story 10).
  - **Golden fixtures.** The golden set covers all 13 languages the anchors
    read. Python `ast` values are recorded for 3.11 through 3.14, because
    they differ between versions. Any change to a fingerprint fails the
    suite until the algorithm version is bumped. An entry stamped under an
    algorithm this DocGuard does not compute is unverifiable, never suspect.
  - **Oracle.** A CI-only job (`tools/anchor-oracle`) measures the pattern
    tier against tree-sitter on a vendored corpus of idiomatic code and the
    anchor fixtures. It fails when a high-confidence language disagrees on
    more than 1% of declarations. Every package in it passes the dependency
    vetting recorded in `VETTING.md` (Kotlin's and Swift's grammars do not,
    so those languages have no oracle). It installs from a lockfile with no
    install scripts, and nothing in it ships.
  - **Tree-sitter tier.** `anchors.treeSitter.artifacts` lets tree-sitter
    refine the span and exact fingerprint of each pattern-tier symbol in Go,
    Rust, Java, C#, PHP, Ruby, C and C++, keeping keys and floors unchanged.
    Only files matching the hashes in
    `schemas/docguard-anchor-treesitter.manifest.json` load. They are staged
    under `.docguard/ts/` and parsed in a child process with no environment,
    never through `node_modules`. Anything missing or mismatched is ANC010,
    and the pattern tier answers.
  - **Pattern tier fixes the oracle found.** These are:
    - Ruby `Const = Struct.new … do` class bodies;
    - Java compact constructors, and annotation elements with defaults;
    - C# expression bodies that span a switch expression;
    - C functions returning `struct x`;
    - C++ inline namespaces, user-defined literal operators, and
      `= delete` / `= default` members.

    On the corpus, every measured language agrees 100% with tree-sitter.
  - **Explicit scope wins.** `{scope=symbol}` in a file's leading comment
    block now anchors the declaration below, as ANC006's advice says. A tag
    inside a `switch` case anchors its statement.
  - **Cache identity.** The anchor cache is keyed by the resolver code and the
    requirement patterns too, so an upgrade or a custom
    `traceability.requirementPattern` is never answered with stale anchors.
- **DocGuard's own requirement tags name their scope.** Every tag that sat
  below an import, inside a function, or in a header directly above a
  declaration now says `{scope=file}`, `{scope=symbol}` or
  `{scope=statement}`. `docguard anchors` on this repository reports no ANC006
  or ANC007, and every link is reviewed or baselined.
- **Release-managed values no longer make requirement links suspect**
  (`docguard.volatile-anchor-lines`). A version string your release tool
  rewrites used to turn every link over its file suspect on every release.
  Mark the line with a `# docguard:volatile` comment:
  - Whatever lies wholly on the marked line is fingerprinted as a placeholder,
    at every tier, so the value can change and the link stays current.
  - Adding or removing the marker is itself a change that a reviewer sees.
  - A file with no marker fingerprints exactly as before.
  - An anchor made only of marked lines is listed as ANC011 by
    `docguard anchors`, never by guard.

  DocGuard marks its own two release-managed lines (`action.yml`,
  `extensions/spec-kit-docguard/extension.yml`), so a release cut leaves
  every anchor as it was.

### Changed

- **The doc lock's fingerprinting moved into a shared module.** It now lives
  in `cli/scanners/fingerprint.mjs`, byte for byte, as `doclock-v0`; every
  accepted section stays current.
  - Covered Python symbols are read in one `python3` run per check instead of
    one per symbol.
  - Member paths resolve at any depth (`Outer.Inner.method`,
    `outer.helper`).
- **Requirement definitions carry their whole `block`.** Every line of a list
  item, heading or paragraph is included, so a requirement fingerprint sees
  every line. `text` stays the first line.

### Fixed

- **Ten TestGuard faults that could not be injected are re-pointed.** TestGuard
  injects a fault only when its `find` text occurs exactly once in its file.
  Ten faults in `testguard.claims.json` matched zero or two times, so their
  claims were weaker than they read. The scanner refactors of 2026-10-10
  (#530, #532–#535, #537, #538) moved or duplicated the lines they pointed at:
  - FALLBACK-LANGUAGE-COVERAGE-IS-PARTIAL F8, F20;
  - PYTHON-EXTRACTION-IS-ACCURATE F1, F19, F28;
  - JS-TS-EXTRACTION-MATCHES-TRUTH F2, F4, F18, F30;
  - GENERATED-DOCS-PASS-OWN-CHECKS F37.

  Each now targets the code that implements the behaviour its description
  names, and every fault in the file matches exactly once. Test-only: no
  shipped behaviour changes.

- **Two `docguard watch` tests no longer race the watcher's output**
  (`docguard.watch-deterministic` FR-004). Each waited on an earlier or weaker
  marker than the line it then asserted, so a slow runner could read the
  header before the next line arrived (CI run 38300989325). Both now wait on
  the pattern they assert; the block passed 10 sequential and 3×4 concurrent
  runs. No sleep added.

- **A quoted `<!--` no longer hides the rest of a spec**
  (`docguard.quoted-comment-openers`). A requirement line that quoted an HTML
  comment opener in backticks, such as ``- **FR-001**: Strip the `<!--`
  marker``, opened a comment that never closed, so every requirement after it
  was dropped without a word: traceability under-counted and tags citing them
  read as citing nothing. Agent instruction files had the same gap for doc
  pointers. A `<!--` inside an inline code span is now text, and real HTML
  comments still hide what they hold. No requirement or pointer on this
  repository changed. Found by the TODO-parsing session (spec 073).

- **Kotlin routes built from a string template are no longer reported at a
  guessed path** (`docguard.go-spring-rails-routes` FR-006). `"\\$v"` (a
  backslash, then the template `$v`) and a raw `"""\$v"""` string (no escapes)
  were read as literal text; both are now templates, so the route is omitted.
  An escaped `"\$v"` stays literal. Found by Jules (#566).

- **A tag quoted inside a string is no longer requirement evidence.** The
  implementation-evidence scanner read `// @req FR-012` inside a help string
  (`cli/commands/explain.mjs`) as a tag. It now reads real comments only, in
  every language it can lex, and quote-aware `#` comments in YAML and shell.
  - **What changes on DocGuard itself.** Four implementation-evidence
    entries that 0.44.3 recorded disappear. Each came from a `/*` inside a
    string (a glob) that the old regex took for the start of a comment,
    swallowing the code after it:
    - `cli/commands/trace.mjs` for `docguard.doc-ownership-map#FR-004`,
      `docguard.mcp-doc-tools#FR-003` and `docguard.output-ux#FR-009`;
    - `cli/findings.mjs` for `docguard.ignore-reasons#FR-005`.

    The spec registry's projection changes accordingly. Guard output is
    otherwise unchanged against 0.44.3 on this repository and on the
    projects in the release gate.
- **A Python interpreter upgrade no longer reads as a code change in the doc
  lock.** A `python-ast` mismatch whose code is unchanged since the reviewed
  revision, re-read with today's interpreter, is now unverifiable instead of
  DLK001.
- **`specs complete --write` no longer rolls back on deviations given out of
  order** (`specs/028-completion-revision-anchoring`, FR-007). Two
  `--deviation` values not already sorted failed with "File transaction
  rolled back: completed registry does not match the resulting repository":
  completion recorded them in the order given, and the projection that
  validates the write sorts them. The same mismatch could hit:
  - deviations that differ only in whitespace, deduplicated before
    normalization;
  - evidence paths whose code-unit and `localeCompare` orders differ, such as
    `README.md` next to `cli/…`.

  Completion now builds its outcome with the projection's own
  `canonicalOutcome`. The spec's outcome line and the plan's evidence list use
  that order too, and the bound of 20 counts distinct deviations. Recorded
  outcomes are unchanged: the registry already stored them in this form.
- **A multi-line import is now an import-graph edge** (`specs/076-js-import-edges`).
  JS/TS imports were read by one pattern whose clause stopped at the end of a
  line, so `import {\n  a,\n  b,\n} from './x.mjs'` (Prettier's style for any
  long import) produced no edge. They are now read from the Babel syntax tree:
  - import declarations of any shape and length, `import type` included;
  - re-exports with a source (`export * from`, `export { … } from`), which load
    their module as an import does and were never read;
